description: Single storey front/side extension to allow for conversion of detached rear garage into single storey, 1-bed, detached dwelling with associated parking and amenity space, involving alterations to front elevation and boundary treatments to front
decision_conditions: The proposed dwelling would not relate to the surrounding garden scene which is characterised by rear gardens and domestic outbuildings.  A self-contained detached dwelling would appear out of character in this back garden environment and it would set a harmful precedent for infilling other similar undeveloped areas present throughout the locality which would erode from and diminish the local character, contrary to Policies 7, 10 and 26 of the Havering Local Plan 2021 and Policies D4 and D6 of the London Plan 2021.

The constraints of the site in conjunction with the design approach adopted would be to the detriment of the amenity of future occupiers. The proposal would lead to poor quality outlook from habitable rooms and low celling heights to the detriment of the future occupiers, contrary to the aims of Policies 7, 10 and 26 of the Havering Local Plan 2021 and Policies D4 and D6 of the London Plan 2021.

The proposed development would by reason of its bulk, mass and scale on a constrained site within close proximity of the boundaries result in an visually intrusive form of development that would compromise the amenity and the enjoyment of the neighbours private outdoor spaces due to the increased sense of enclosure created by the proposal, contrary to Policies 7, 10 and 26 of the Havering Local Plan 2021 and Policies D4 and D6 of the London Plan 2021.

The proposed development would appear to be in close proximity to existing trees. No tree plan has been submitted nor any details of tree mitigation or protection measures. Consequently, insufficient information has been submitted to be able to conclude that the proposal would not have a harmful impact on existing trees and landscape, contrary to Policy 27 of the Local Plan.

In the absence of measures to ensure that the proposal is a self-build dwelling, it is not considered that the Biodiversity Net Gain requirements have been satisfied. Note: there is currently no "small site" exemption.

The proposal, if granted planning permission on appeal, would be liable for the Mayor of London and Havering Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL). Based upon the information supplied with the application, the CIL payable would be £740 and £3700. Further details with regard to CIL are available from the Council's website.

Statement Required by Article 35 (2) of the Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015: Consideration was given to seeking amendments, but given conflict with adopted planning policy, it was necessary to issue a decision as close to the statutory timeframe as possible as opposed to seeking amendments which would have significantly delayed the application.
